a: Server stores session; browser sends session cookie on each request.
JWT has header.payload.signature — verify signature and expiry always.
JWTs are often stateless; sessions are server-side and easier to revoke.
Rotate refresh tokens on use to reduce replay risk if stolen.
Passwordless uses email magic links, OTP, or WebAuthn instead of passwords.
WebAuthn enables phishing-resistant auth with platform/security keys.
Client credentials flow is machine-to-machine without a user login.
OIDC adds identity (ID token) on top of OAuth 2.0 authorization.
SAML is an XML-based SSO standard common in enterprises.
RBAC assigns permissions to roles, then roles to users.
ABAC grants access based on attributes (user, resource, context).
MFA methods include TOTP apps, SMS (weaker), hardware keys, push approve.
